ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, D and E are the midpoints of sides AB and AC of $\triangle ABC$, respectively. CD and BE intersect at point O. What is the value of $\frac{S_{\triangle COE}}{S_{\triangle BOC}}$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Since $D$ and $E$ are the midpoints of sides $AB$ and $AC$ of $\triangle ABC$ respectively,\\
it follows that $DE \parallel BC$ and $DE = \frac{1}{2}BC$,\\
thereby $\triangle DOE \sim \triangle COB$,\\
which implies $\frac{DE}{BC}=\frac{OE}{OB}=\frac{1}{2}$,\\
resulting in ${S}_{\triangle COE}:{S}_{\triangle BOC}=\frac{OE}{OB}=\boxed{\frac{1}{2}}$;

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure is triangle ABC, with B at the lower left, C at the lower right, and A above; point D is located on side AB, and point E is located on side AC; segment CD and segment BE intersect at point O inside the triangle. Reasoning: The problem gives that D and E are respectively the midpoints of AB and AC, therefore CD is the median from C to the midpoint of AB, and BE is the median from B to the midpoint of AC. The two medians intersect at O, so O is the centroid of triangle ABC. The centroid divides median BE in the ratio from the vertex to the midpoint, that is, BO:OE = 2:1, therefore OE/OB = 1/2. If triangles COE and BOC take OE and OB as bases respectively, these two bases are on the same straight line BE, and their other vertex is the same C, so the heights to line BE are the same. Thus the area ratio equals the base ratio: S_{triangle COE}/S_{triangle BOC} = OE/OB = 1/2.
